tables.title: The week in three parts — each vs the same weekdays one week earlier
tables.note: Mon 09-14 carries the v1722 publish at 16:09 UTC, so the week splits into a pre-v1722 weekend and a post-v1722 Tue–Wed. D1 for a day needs the next day, so its newest pairs are included only where served.
tables.source: Corpus `series.json` ONE_DAY headline series (IsNewUser rows are the `DailyActiveUsers` filter slices); CCU = mean of 24 settled hourly `ConcurrentPlayers` buckets (Open Cloud pull 09-19 09:01Z). Each cell = mean(after days) ÷ mean(same weekdays −7d) − 1.

tables.title: Did any publish change concurrents beyond the normal time-of-day swing?
columns: Same clock slots, non-publish days: mean
tables.note: Before = the six half-hours ending at the publish slot; after = six half-hours starting one hour after it (skips the restart dip/spike). A z near 0 means the publish day moved like any other day at that clock time.
tables.source: `PeakConcurrentPlayers` HALF_HOUR (Open Cloud pull 09-19 09:01Z, start-labelled). Base = every day 08-23→09-18 without a publish (08-28, 09-04, 09-11, 09-14, 09-17 excluded).

tables.title: Three new-world launches, same test: the five days after vs the same weekdays one week earlier
tables.note: The spec blocks for 07.08, 28.08 and 10.09 all read 'NEW WORLD — 7 rafts, 2 limited pets, 3 eggs, 3 trails'. Only the third launch is followed by a rise.
tables.source: Event dates from `ANNOTATION_TYPE_EXPERIENCE_EVENT_STATE` (NEW WORLD START); specs in `data/updates/10030829154-climb-waterslide-and-slide.md`. Corpus ONE_DAY headline series; peak DAU 688,061 on 2026-08-02.

tables.title: Where the DAU change came from: impressions × impression→play conversion, per weekday pair
columns: Residual (DAU not covered by impr × CVR)
tables.note: On the weekend DAU rose while impressions fell — the gain was all conversion. From Monday both terms rose. The total row is the geometric mean of the five pair ratios.
tables.source: Corpus ONE_DAY `DailyActiveUsers`, `UniqueUsersWithImpressions`, `EndToEndCVR`. Share = log(term ratio) ÷ log(DAU ratio); residual = DAU ratio ÷ (impressions ratio × CVR ratio).

tables.title: Thumbnail swaps against the base rate of ordinary days
tables.note: Same statistic on every day with no swap on it or either neighbour gives the base rate. The 'all swaps' z uses the standard error of a mean. Only one swap day is flagged per UTC date. The images were not inspected for this read. The 09-08 swap's z of +2.47 has a one-sided p of 0.0067 on its own; the chance that at least one of 24 swap days reaches it by chance is 0.15.
tables.source: `ANNOTATION_TYPE_PLACE_THUMBNAIL` rows in `data/games/10030829154/annotations.md`; corpus `RFYPlayThroughRate` and `UniqueUsersWithImpressions` ONE_DAY; base days 05-08→09-17.

tables.title: The eight Home-ranking signals by day, against impressions
tables.note: Roblox documents that an impression change usually FOLLOWS a move in these signals. Read the columns top to bottom for which moved first: the reach step is 09-14/09-15.

tables.title: D1 by acquisition source: effect size (relative change) and confidence (z) kept apart
tables.note: Friends arrive by invite and never see a thumbnail; Search looked the game up. z vs own sd = Δ ÷ (sd·√(2/5)), the standard error of a difference of two 5-day means. Relative Δ is the composition instrument; z says whether it moved at all.
tables.source: Corpus `ForwardD1Retention` ONE_DAY by `AcquisitionSource` (5/5 pairs); n = `UniqueUsersWithPlaySessions` by `AcquisitionSource`, `IsNewUser=New`.

tables.title: How much of the D1 rise is traffic mix and how much is within-source
rows: Rates before, mix after (mix effect only)
Mix before, rates after (within-source effect only)
tables.note: Weights are each source's new players per day. The four sources carry ~99% of new players; the blend reproduces the headline D1 closely.
tables.source: Corpus `ForwardD1Retention` by `AcquisitionSource` and `UniqueUsersWithPlaySessions` by `AcquisitionSource` (`IsNewUser=New`), 5 paired weekdays each side.

tables.title: Returning players against what the last seven days of new cohorts predict
columns: Expected returners from cohorts aged 1–7 days
tables.note: Model: expected = Σ New(t−k) × r_k, k = 1…7, with r_k the day-k cohort retention averaged over 08-20→09-06 (r1 13.0%, r2 6.0%, r3 3.2%, r4 2.0%, r5 1.3%, r6 1.0%, r7 0.8%). If the new world pulled lapsed players back, the 'everyone else' column rises from 09-12. It is a model, not a measurement of individual players.
tables.source: Corpus `DailyActiveUsers` filtered `IsNewUser=New` / `Returning` (slices), `DailyCohortRetention` by `CohortDay` (sparse: CohortDay k served for 5–14 cohort dates each).

tables.title: Session length and playtime: within-segment change vs the shift toward new players
tables.note: Weights are DAU by segment (a session-weighted blend would differ slightly for session length). New players play fewer minutes per day, so a week with twice the new players pulls playtime per DAU down with no change to either group.
tables.source: Explore (`dag/execute`) `AverageSessionLengthMinutes`, `AveragePlayTimeMinutesPerDAU` and `DailyActiveUsers` by `IsNewUser`, paired weekday means (5/5); headline from the corpus.

tables.title: Revenue = DAU × paying-user CVR × ARPPU, by part of the week
tables.note: Shares are of the log-change in revenue and can exceed 100% when another term moved the other way. The three terms multiply back to revenue up to rounding in Roblox's own daily figures.
tables.source: Corpus ONE_DAY `DailyRevenue`, `DailyActiveUsers`, `PayingUsersCVR`, `AverageRevenuePerPayingUser`; weekday-paired means.

tables.title: Matched-DAU check: each post-build day against the earlier day with the closest DAU
tables.note: Holds audience size fixed so the payer count is compared at the same scale. The matched days sit in August, when the audience had a different age and country mix, so this bounds rather than isolates.
tables.source: Corpus ONE_DAY `DailyActiveUsers`, `PayingUsers`, `DailyRevenue`; nearest absolute DAU among 07-20→09-10.

tables.title: Item revenue per concurrent-player-hour, by day
tables.note: Revenue per hour of play rather than per player, from one read so every hour carries the same restatement lag (the newest hours are the least settled). Sanity check: the daily sums of this hourly read ÷ `DailyRevenue` over 09-05→09-16 run 1.00–1.01. The last two rows are the only readable money signal for v1723, whose behavioural metrics are not served yet.
tables.source: Raw bundle `data/raw/10030829154-2026-09-19T09-01-24-481Z.json`, `ItemMonetizationRevenue` ONE_HOUR by `ProductType`; hourly `ConcurrentPlayers` (Open Cloud pull 09-19 09:01Z); ARPDAU = corpus `AverageRevenuePerUser`.

tables.title: Cohort maturity: the same comparison under three reads

tables.note: Cohort rates keep rising for days as players come back. The first read favours POST here (its cohorts were read older); the same-day read favours PRE; the third read is the closest to age-matched. A move that keeps its sign under all three is not a maturity artefact.
tables.source: Corpus first reads (`capturedAt` per point) and the two raw bundles `data/raw/10030829154-2026-09-19T09-01-24-481Z.json` and `…-2026-09-14T16-54-33-273Z.json` (`FunnelCohortCompletionRate`, `FunnelName=TutorialFunnel`, ONE_DAY). Age = read time − end of cohort day.

The price-lookup failures carry the same client call path as before (`ProductMgr.GetProductPrice` from `UI.HUD` line 110) but at ProductMgr line 133 instead of 125, and one row adds a call from `GoShop_Raft.setSpeedDisplay` — which is why a long-standing message is filed under v1723. tables.note: A review can carry several themes. The raft-shop theme needs both a raft/shop word and a scroll/broken word (several languages). The n is small: say it with every number. columns: DAU change, day +1 vs same weekday −7
tables.note: `RSVPCount` is cumulative (1.1M) and occasionally jumps by ~205K in one day (a batch roll-up on 08-14 and 08-21), so only small daily increments are read. Increments of a few hundred to ~2,000 a day are three orders below the DAU moves.

tables.title: Waterslide against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep
tables.note: 1.00 = this game moved exactly like the rest of the portfolio that day; below 1 = worse, above 1 = better (for crash rate, above 1 = more crashes). Each game is first divided by its own 01–07 Sep mean, so shared calendar or platform effects — the 08 Sep payer step, the Labor Day weekend — cancel. Rates are the reliable rows; for DAU and impressions the peers mix growing and decaying games, so read those rows as 'moved differently from the portfolio', not as a counterfactual.
tables.source: `run` series in reports/2026-09-19/data/<slug>.json (settled ONE_DAY headline). Index = (this game ÷ its own 01–07 Sep mean) ÷ median over the other four games of the same ratio. tools/r0919/peer-index.js
